描述_EN: A blue and white glaze incised phoenix-head pot from the Xicun kilns，the Song dynasty (960-1279)，your (honorific)16.8centimetre，caliber4.2centimetre，footsteps8.4centimetre。　　with a phoenix-shaped mouth，your (honorific)冠，big eyes，varicose bill，Crested corolla as water filler。Three strings protruding from the long neck，lit. round belly, full stomach，wide-rimmed foot。A long, curved stream on one shoulder，Cylindrical handle on the other side，stream of water or sth. resembling one、The handle is a back repair。Green and white glaze on all sides，Thin glaze。The upper part of the outer wall of the abdomen is engraved with entwined floral motifs，The lower part is engraved with banana leaf pattern。　　　　Although the shape of this phoenix head pot originated from Sui Dynasty, it is not a very popular one.、Wares influenced by Persian styles during the Tang period，But its belly has its own unique style。the Sui dynasty (581-617 AD)、Tang-period phoenix-head pots with elongated abdomens，and stacked with ornamentation on top of it，The belly of this pot is rounded and bulging，Decorated with incised flowers。Comparison with the specimens collected from the kiln site survey shows that，This bottle is from a kiln in Xicun, Guangdong。　　Nishimura kiln porcelain was mainly used for exporting，Currently, there are fewer excavations and heirlooms in China.，In contrast, there are large numbers of excavations around Southeast Asia, especially in the Philippines。
描述_ZN: A large bowl with a phoenix pattern carved in brown and white glaze from Xicun kiln, Song dynasty, 8.9 cm high, 33.3 cm in diameter, 9.5 cm in foot diameter.　　Bowl folded rim, curved wall, ring foot. The whole body is glazed with green and white glaze. The inner bottom carved phoenix pattern, and decorated with five groups of regular brown dot color. The inner wall engraved lotus flower pattern, flower pattern on the random dotted brown dot color. Bowl outer wall plain surface without decoration.　　This bowl is large and regular in shape, decorated with a combination of engraved flowers and dotted color, complex but not chaotic, a masterpiece of the Song Dynasty Xicun kiln porcelain.　　The blue and white glaze carved with brown dots is a unique variety of Xicun kiln. This technique has been found in the blue-glazed ware excavated from the Jin tomb in Guangzhou, so it can be seen that it was handed down from the Jin Dynasty.
